title: L-carnosine physical performance: overall nulls with two exploratory subgroup signals
disposition: Retain bounded human functional comparator; no broad strength/endurance efficacy or nomination replacement established
dose: 2 g/day orally: four 0.5-g capsules, two twice daily, for about 12 weeks
formulation_limit: The 2020 protocol planned BulkSupplements L-carnosine compounded into gelatin capsules at the University of Colorado; final batch not verified. Not beta-alanine, zinc-carnosine or a mixture.
population: Louisville-area adults aged 22–65 with low urinary carnosine, mean age about 45; not selected for neuromuscular disease or weakness.

analysis.primary_outcome: Vascular and circulating-cell measures, not physical function
analysis.overall_physical_comparisons: All seven overall comparisons were null at both visits; age/sex-adjusted mixed-model coefficients were null.
nominal_positives: All participants ≤40: calf raise at visit 3, coefficient 0.102 (95% CL 0.016–0.189), P=.018
Men >40: step test at visit 4, coefficient 0.074 (95% CL 0.016–0.132), P=.010
analysis.prespecification: Physical tests were planned; age/sex subgroup interest appears in the 2020 SAP. Exact ≤40/>40 cutoff prespecification was not verified; randomization strata were 22–44/45–65.

molecular_fidelity.scope: Complete scientific main and supplement; not proof about undisclosed data.

counterevidence.result: 49 randomized, 43 completed; 2 g/day for 14 weeks. Grip, relative grip, body composition and bone measures did not differ versus placebo.
SAMR1 mouse aberrant spermatogonia/spermatids increased by 64%/85% by micronucleus assay; SAMP1 result null. Dose, route, denominators and statistical details unread.
counterevidence.limit: No human genotoxicity or BUBR1-causal claim.

competition: Retain real between-group functional measurements. Active-only adherence/response exclusions, overall nulls, multiplicity and absent subgroup interaction evidence prevent a strong nominee challenge. Apply the same causal caution to niacin open-label strength; apitegromab has a distinct SMA primary motor context. No comparative MVA efficacy is proved.
